# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 15 (LOGOS Formal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 15
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Moreover, concerning the Sabbath it is also written in the Ten Commandments, in which he spoke to Moses face to face on Mount Sinai: "Sanctify also the Sabbath of the Lord with clean hands and a pure heart."
2. And in another place he says: "If my sons guard the Sabbath, then I will bestow my mercy upon them."
3. The Sabbath is mentioned at the beginning of the creation: "And God made the works of his hands in six days, and he finished on the seventh day and rested in it and sanctified it."
4. Take note, children, what "he finished in six days" means. This means: in six thousand years the Lord will bring all things to a conclusion; for a day with him signifies a thousand years, and he himself bears witness, saying: "Behold, the day of the Lord will be as a thousand years." Therefore, children, in six days — that is, in six thousand years — all things will be brought to completion.
5. "And he rested on the seventh day." This signifies: when his Son comes he will put an end to the time of the Lawless One and will judge the ungodly, and will transform the sun and the moon and the stars — then he will truly rest on the seventh day.
6. Furthermore he says: "Sanctify it with clean hands and a pure heart." If therefore anyone is at present able to make holy that day which God has made holy, being pure in heart, we are altogether deceived.
7. Behold, therefore: we shall truly rest and sanctify it at that time, when we ourselves shall be able to do so — having been made righteous ourselves, having received the promise, when there shall be no more iniquity, and all things shall have been made new by the Lord. Then we shall be able to sanctify it, having first been made holy ourselves.
8. Furthermore he says to them: "Your new moons and your sabbaths I cannot endure." You see what he means: it is not the present sabbaths that are acceptable to me, but the one which I have made — in which, when I have given rest to all things, I will make a beginning of the eighth day, that is, the beginning of another world.
9. For this reason also we keep the eighth day as a day of gladness — the day on which Jesus rose from the dead, and when he had appeared, he ascended into the heavens.
